Saraswathi vs B.M.T.C on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198642415/
1
This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Smt Saraswathi in the Road Traffic Accident dated 31.03.2023.

2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
That on 31.03.2023 at about 10.45 a.m., petitioner being a passenger of a BMTC Volvo bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-129 has come from Shivaji nagar and when petitioner got down from the said bus near Corporation circle and proceeding to cross the road very carefully and cautiously observing the traffic rules and regulations.
At that time, all of a sudden another BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-2572 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and hit SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2546/2023 the petitioner.

Due to which, petitioner fell down and BMTC volvo bus suddenly moved in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering the human life at high speed and the right side back wheel of the said bus ran over the right leg of the petitioner.
Due to which, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries to the whole body.

3. Immediately, after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Victoria Hospital and after first aid treatment she was shifted to Sparsh hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient.

Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4.
In pursuance of service of the notice respondent appeared through its Counsel and filed Objections to the claim petition.

The Respondent has filed written statement submitting as follows:
SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2546/2023 It is submitted by the respondent that the petitioner herself was tortfeasor and the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the petitioner.
Further submitted that this respondent is not at all responsible for the alleged accident.
It is submitted that the amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive, arbitrary, unreasonable and without any legal basis.
Hence, on these grounds, Respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 13.02.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 31.03.2023 at about 10.45 a.m., In front of Corporation bus stop, Corporation circle, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-2572?

Saraswathi vs B.M.T.C on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198642415/
2 SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2546/2023 2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3) What Order or Award?

RECASTED ISSUE 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 31.03.2023 at about 10.45 a.m., In front of Corporation bus stop, Corporation circle, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the drivers of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-2572 and BMTC Volvo bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-129?
6.

In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 20 documents and respondent examined one witness as RW.1.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Recasted Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order
for the following :
REASONS 8.
Recasted Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-2572 and Reg.No.KA-57-F-129.
9.

In this regard the petitioner got herself examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination she has deposed that on 31.03.2023 at about 6.30 p.m., she was passenger of BMTC Volvo bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-129 and was coming from Shivaji nagar and when the bus stopped in front of SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2546/2023 Corporation bus stop she got down from the bus and was about to cross the road and all of a sudden offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner at high speed Saraswathi vs B.M.T.C on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198642415/
3 and hit the petitioner.

Due to which, she fell down and at that time the driver of the BMTC volvo bus suddenly moved the bus in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life at high speed and the right side back wheel of the said bus ran over the right leg of the petitioner.
Due to which, she sustained multiple fractures and crushed and degloving injury.
10. The petitioner in support of her claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR filed against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and Sec.134(a&b) and 187 of MV Act on the basis of the complaint given by husband of the petitioner on 31.03.2023.
Ex.P3 is the spot mahazar which discloses the spot of the accident and the spot sketch discloses that the accident took SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2546/2023 place near Corporation bus stop.
Ex.P5 is the wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to the impact of the accident.

Ex.P6 is the charge sheet filed against the drivers of both buses for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.134(a&b) and 187 of MV Act and contents of the charge sheet discloses that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent of the both the bus drivers.

Hence,
these documents satisfactorily establish that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of the both buses.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW1 is cross examined by the learned counsel for respondent and in her cross examination she has deposed that the accident took place in front of Corporation road in the middle of the road and there is bus stop in front of corporation and there is foot path on either side of the road.

PW.1 deposed that she came from Shivajinagar and got down from the bus from the front door and other passengers also got down and had to SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2546/2023 go to go to cotton pet market and she went in front of the bus in order to the other side and at that time another bus was coming from behind which she did not notice when she was about cross the road from the front of the bus, the bus from which she got down dashed her and the wheel of the bus ran over her leg resulting in the accident.

She has deposed that there was distance of 2 feet between both the buses and left side of the bus touched her, as a result she fell down and the tyre of the bus went over her leg, resulting in grievous injuries.
In her further cross-examination she has denied that she herself negligently crossed the road resulting in the accident.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner's side, nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross- SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2546/2023 examination of Respondent.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also denied the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident due to their own negligence.

The fact that the rider of the offending vehicles have already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.134(a&b) and 187 of MV Saraswathi vs B.M.T.C on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198642415/
4 Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.

The certified copies of FIR,
charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of drivers of both vehicles at the relevant time.

Hence, Recasted issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2546/2023 12. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.
13. MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:
PW.2 has produced inpatient details and the petitioner has also produced Ex.P5 wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries due to the accident.

Ex.P7 is the discharge summary which discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment in Sparsh hospital from 31.03.2023 to 14.04.2023 and produced Ex.P8 - medical bills 46 in nos. and Ex.P9 are the Advance receipts.
Ex.P10 are the prescriptions and Ex.P11 are the Lab reports.
As far as the medical bills and treatment is concerned PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner herself has paid the hospital expenses and denied that the medical bills are reimbursed through insurance.
PW.1 has deposed that she has produced original bills and stated that she does not have any health insurance.
SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2546/2023 Nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
Hence in view of the medical bills produced the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.7,63,808/- under the head medical bills.
14. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and Ex.P5 discloses that the petitioner has sustained degloving injury right lower limb and fracture of right medial malleolus and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and she cannot do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain the quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the trauma, pain and sufferings etc., which she actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded to her towards pain and SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2546/2023 sufferings.
Thus, she is awarded an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In her evidence PW.1 has submitted she was aged about 47 years and she was running general store and doing tailoring work and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
In her cross-examination she has admitted that she has not produced any document to prove her avocation and income.
In addition the petitioner has also not produced any business license or bank statement or income tax returns or business accounts to prove her income and avocation.

Since there is no satisfactory evidence to prove the said income and avocation of the petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the Saraswathi vs B.M.T.C on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198642415/
5 accident.

As per the minimum wages chart and the lok adalath chart the income for the said avocation for the relevant period is ranging between Rs.14,000 to 15,000/- and hence the notional income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Taking into consideration that SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2546/2023 the petitioner due to the injuries might not have been in a position to work for at least 9 months hence
, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,000 X 9 = 1,44,000/- under this head.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:

The petitioner has claimed in her affidavit she has permanent disability and as per the evidence of PW.2 her impairment is not progressive and will not improve in future and hence it is submitted by the petitioner that she cannot pursue her work as before the accident.

As far as the disability is concerned petitioner has got examined PW.3 - Orthopedic Surgeon and in his evidence he has deposed that the petitioner has undergone surgeries in the form of wound debridement + VAC dressing + SSG for skin avulsion under SA, Right medical malleolus - ORIF under SA and LD muscle flap + SSG under GA and has complains of pain and difficulty in walking and climbing stairs and cannot SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2546/2023 squat and sitting cross legged and there is gross wasting of the right leg is seen depressed scars and contractures are seen.
Deformed right ankle is noted and she needs another surgery for removal of implants.

He has assessed total disability of the petitioner to right lower limb at 52%
and whole body disability at 26%.

PW.3 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for respondent, wherein he has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and denied that knee pain is due to age factor and stated that he has assessed the disability on the basis of gonia meter.

As far as the functional disability is concerned the petitioner has stated she doing tailoring and if the said avocation is taken into consideration then the disability has certainly effected her avocation.
Hence the said disability assessed can be taken as 1/3 to the whole body, 1/3 of 52% is 17.3% which is taken as disability to assess the compensation payable to the petitioner.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.16,000/- at the relevant time.

As far as, age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2546/2023 concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P15 the date of birth of the petitioner is 30.08.1976.

Going by the same,
the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 31.03.2023 was around 47 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

sentences.text:
SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '13'
is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of her above disability.

The loss of future earnings of petitioner due to above injury and permanent physical disability comes to Rs.4,31,808/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 13 X 17.3%) and the same is awarded to him as compensation under this head.

Saraswathi vs B.M.T.C on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198642415/
6 17.
Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical SCCH 15 17 MVC No.2546/2023 disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

18. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that she might have taken the help of an attendant.
Further, she would be requiring conveyance for movement.
Her avocation has been hit due to her disablement.
She might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during her treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
19. COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
It is stated in the evidence of PW.3 that Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of the implant.
But he has not produced estimation.
However, by considering the need for further surgery, it is proper to grant compensation of SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2546/2023 20,000/-.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

20. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  1,00,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  50,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid  1,44,000/-
up period 4.

Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  1,00,000/-
and conveyance 5. Medical expenses 7,63,808/-
6. Loss of Future Income 4,31,808/-
7.

Future medical expenses  20,000/-
Total 16,09,616/-
Saraswathi vs B.M.T.C on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198642415/
7 Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 16,09,616/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. RAJASTAN VS. SMT.
LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

sentences.text: Hence the rate of interest is set at 6% per annum in this case.
22. Regarding Liability:

As far as the liability is concerned the driver of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-2572 is examined as RW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that he was proceeding from Shivajinagar to K.R. Market and near Corporation bus stop the petitioner got down and wanted to go to cottonpet and all of a sudden crossed the main road from front side of the bus and came in contact with the front portion of the bus and fell down and at that time the bus went over her right leg, resulting in the injuries.
It is SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2546/2023 submitted that he was driving carefully and it is because of the negligence of the petitioner in crossing the road, the accident occurred.

RW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the petitioner he has admitted that after passengers get down and after verifying he has to proceed forward and admitted that petitioner was passenger and got down from his bus.
He has deposed that there was no zebra cross at the accident spot.
RW.1 has denied that the accident occurred due to his negligence since without noticing the road he took the bus all of a sudden and dashed the petitioner.
Hence, the main contention taken by the respondent is that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of KA-57-F-2572.
However, respondent have not got examined the other bus driver of KA- 57-F-129.

As far as the investigation is concerned the charge sheet is filed against drivers of the both the buses and hence on the basis of the evidence there is negligence on the part of the both the drivers of the buses.

Both the bus drivers ought to have been cautiously and notice the passengers who board SCCH 15 21 MVC No.2546/2023 and get down from the bus and proceed towards other directions after getting down from the bus.

Therefore, the Respondent who is internal insurer of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-2572 and Volvo bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57- 0219 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
23. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of 16,09,616/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.

LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
As far as the investigation is concerned the charge sheet is filed against drivers of the both the buses and hence on the basis of the evidence there is negligence on the part of the both the drivers of the buses.
Both the bus drivers ought to have been cautiously and notice the passengers who board SCCH 15 21 MVC No.2546/2023 and get down from the bus and proceed towards other directions after getting down from the bus.
Therefore, the Respondent who is internal insurer of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-2572 and Volvo bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57- 0219 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
